newsitem.title: USA: Dr. Jack Kevorkian is arrested in Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Dr. Jack Kevorkian is arrested in Michigan.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian remained jailed on Thursday following his arrest earlier in the day and was likely to face new charges for assisting in a woman's suicide in a small central Michigan town in August, his lawyer said.
Kevorkian's attorney, Geoffrey Fieger, condemned the arrest as "despicable" and said it was political grandstanding by Ionia County Prosecutor Raymond Vote.
The case involves Loretta Peabody, 54, of Ionia who died on Aug. 30 with Kevorkian's help, although his role was not known until police confiscated a videotape from Kevorkian in a September raid.

Earlier this week Fieger held a news conference with Peabody's husband and daughter at which he played videotapes of Peabody, who suffered from multiple sclerosis, saying she could not endure her suffering any longer and wanted to die.

"I've fought this as long as I can fight this," Peabody was heard saying. Her husband and daughter asked that authorities leave the case alone. Her death brought to 45 the number of deaths Kevorkian has admitted to attending since 1990.
Thursday morning Kevorkian was handcuffed and arrested by plainclothes police while shopping in suburban Waterford Township.

Salesman Jason Whitten at the National Pawn Broker's Outlet said Kevorkian was at the store looking at electronic keyboards shortly before he was arrested. Kevorkian was a regular customer who played the organ, Whitten said.
"I noticed that he was surrounded by some gentlemen (outside the store) who handcuffed him and escorted him into a van," Whitten said.
Fieger complained that Kevorkian was manhandled despite never having missed a court hearing in any previous case.

"Early this morning, secretly, this low-down dog of a prosecutor in Ionia sent plainclothesmen to wrestle Dr. Kevorkian down to the ground ... (They proceeded to) handcuff him and throw him in the back of a police car and drive him handcuffed back to Ionia," Fieger told reporters outside a Detroit courthouse where he was defending an unrelated case.

Last week outgoing Oakland County Prosecutor Richard Thompson, who has failed in two previous attempts to convict Kevorkian, brought another case against the suicide rights crusader. Kevorkian was released on bond.
Thompson's successor, David Gorcyca, says it is unlikely he would pursue the prosecution when he takes office in January.
